text:
I love you at ten in the morning, and at eleven, and at noon. I love you with all my soul and all my body, sometimes, on rainy afternoons. But at two in the afternoon, or at three, when I start thinking about the two of us, and you are thinking about food or daily work or the amusements you don't have, I begin to hate you inwardly, with half the hatred I keep for myself.


Then I love you again, when we lie down and I feel you were made for me, that somehow your knee and belly tell me so, that my hands convince me of it, and that there's no better place for me to come, for me to go, than your body. You come to meet me with your whole self, and we both disappear for an instant, go into the mouth of God, until I tell you I'm hungry or sleepy.


Every day I love you and hate you beyond remedy. And there are days too, hours, when I don't know you, when you're as strange to me as another man's wife. I worry about men, I worry about myself, my sorrows distract me. I may not think of you for a long time. You see. Who could love you less than I do, my love?

translation.title: I Love You at Ten in the Morning
